cum-verifici-permisiuni-aplicatii-telefo.excerpt: Camera, microphone, location and contacts are sensitive data. Review permissions in Android or iPhone settings and grant access only when required by app function. Repeat the check periodically for all installed apps.
cum-verifici-permisiuni-aplicatii-telefo.seo_title: How to check app permissions on your phone
cum-verifici-permisiuni-aplicatii-telefo.title: How to check app permissions on your phone
cum-verifici-permisiuni-aplicatii-telefo.meta_description: Review app access to your camera, microphone, location, contacts, and photos on Android and iPhone.
cum-verifici-permisiuni-aplicatii-telefo.content:
Permissions control what information and features an app can use. Location access may be required for navigation, and the camera and microphone for calls, but not every app needs permanent access. Review permissions after installing apps and from time to time; newer systems can automatically reset access to unused apps.

Start with sensitive permissions

Check location, camera, microphone, contacts, photos, SMS, calendar and access to notifications. Ask yourself what function is actually using that access. If a flashlight app asks for contacts or SMS, deny permission and check for a credible explanation. A legitimate application may request access at a specific time; you can only grant while you use it, when the option exists.

Android

In Settings look for Privacy > Permission Manager or look directly for "Permissions". Open each category and review the approved applications. Android displays, depending on version, a dashboard that shows recent access and can automatically reset inactive app permissions. Menu names and location differ by manufacturer; use the search in Settings if you can't find the indicated path.

iPhone

Open Settings > Privacy & Security and choose the category, for example Location Services, Camera, Microphone, Contacts or Photos. You can revoke access for each app and, in some categories, grant selective access. System indicators show when the camera or microphone is in use; App Privacy Report can help review activity, if available and enabled.

What to do when an app refuses to work

Some features even depend on the requested permission: a map app needs location for navigation, and a call app needs a microphone. You can grant temporary access when using the feature, then revoke it. If the explanation doesn't match the function, look for the developer's documentation or choose an alternative. Avoid granting permanent access just to close a warning window.

Revoking permission does not delete data that the app has already collected or sent to the server. See your account settings and privacy policy if you want to request data deletion. Remove unused apps, update your phone, and install apps only from trusted sources.

cum-recunosti-video-deepfake.excerpt: A deepfake can imitate a person's face or voice, but visual clues do not provide a sure verdict. Check the source, look for independent confirmations and don't send money just based on an emotional appeal.
cum-recunosti-video-deepfake.seo_title: How to recognize a deepfake and verify the source
cum-recunosti-video-deepfake.title: How to recognize a deepfake video
cum-recunosti-video-deepfake.meta_description: Understand what a deepfake is, what clues can help, and why you should verify the source before sharing or acting.
cum-recunosti-video-deepfake.content:
A deepfake is audio, image or video content created or modified with artificial intelligence techniques to imitate a person. It can be used in jokes, artwork, or impersonation scams. Quality varies, and a clip that's short, compressed, or shot in low light can look unusual without being fake. No single visual sign provides a sure verdict.

Clues worth checking out

Some clips may have unnatural mouth movements, inconsistent shadows, jittery edges around the face, imperfect voice-to-image synchronization, or details that change between frames. Audio recordings may have unusual rhythm, breathing, or intonation. These cues are imperfect: compression, camera, lighting, and video connection can produce similar artifacts, and generation tools are improving.

Check provenance, not just pixels

  • Search for the clip or statement on the official channel of the person or institution.
  • Check if reliable media organizations have independently reported the same thing.
  • Use reverse image search for key frames and look for an older version of the clip.
  • Confirm requests for money or information with an already saved number or another known person.
  • Don't redistribute the clip just because it seems urgent or shocking.

Voice or video fraud

An attacker can imitate the voice of a relative asking for urgent help or a supposed executive requesting a transfer. Before any payment, hang up and call the person at a known number. The family can set a verification phrase for emergencies, but it must be kept private. An institution should not ask for your bank password, authentication code or installation of a remote application in a video call.

Limits of automatic detection

Tools that claim to detect any deepfake can give false positives or false negatives. Don't upload a private or sensitive clip to an unknown site just to get a score. Context, source, and confirmation through a separate channel are often more useful for a practical decision than a detector without a public methodology.

If a deepfake is used to ask for money or impersonate someone, keep the URL, time and messages and report the platform content. Contact the bank if you transferred money and the authorities if there is harm or threat. Do not claim that a material is fake until you have sufficient evidence; describe what you have verified and what remains uncertain.

date-personale-nu-introduce-instrumente-.excerpt: Treat prompts as information you send to an online service. It avoids identifiers, passwords, codes, confidential documents and financial information and checks product settings and policy before use.
date-personale-nu-introduce-instrumente-.seo_title: What personal data not to enter in AI tools
date-personale-nu-introduce-instrumente-.title: What Personal Data You Shouldn't Enter in ChatGPT or Other AI Tools
date-personale-nu-introduce-instrumente-.meta_description: Protect passwords, documents, financial data and confidential information when using ChatGPT or other AI tools.
date-personale-nu-introduce-instrumente-.content:
A prompt sent to an AI tool is sent to an online service for processing. How data is kept, reviewed or used depends on the product, account type, active settings and terms of service. Don't assume a conversation is private just because it doesn't appear in a search engine. If in doubt, anonymize the information or use a tool approved by your organization.

Do not enter secrets that provide access

Do not send passwords, unique codes, recovery codes, API keys, PINs or security questions. These values ​​allow direct access to accounts and systems. For technical help, replace them with dummy tags like [TOKEN] and delete the actual data from the screenshots before attaching them.

Limits identification and financial data

Avoid CNP, document series and number, full address, card number, CVV, IBAN associated with sensitive transactions and bank documents. Do not upload invoices, statements, medical records or contracts containing names and signatures unless you have the authority and a clear need. If you want to analyze a text, remove names, numbers, addresses and identifiers before sending it.

Work documents and intellectual property

Do not paste private source code, customer data, business strategies, credentials, or documents marked confidential into a personal account. Check employer policies and workspace settings: Organization accounts may have different retention, administration, and access policies. A button to disable model training is not equivalent to deleting conversations and does not replace data classification rules.

Check service settings

In ChatGPT, OpenAI provides controls for using conversations to enhance models, export, delete, and Temporary Chat; availability depends on plan and workspace. Temporary Chat does not appear in history and is not used to improve models while it remains temporary, but may be kept for a limited time for security reasons, according to the current documentation. Read the official page before entering work or personal data.

AI can produce wrong answers, so do not use the result as an official verification of a contract, diagnosis or bank transfer. For useful prompts, describe the problem with dummy data and keep only the strictly necessary context. If you accidentally sent a password or token, turn it over immediately and review the activity of the associated account.

protejeaza-card-bancar-cumparaturi-onlin.excerpt: Buy from merchants you can verify, use payment methods with dispute procedures and enable bank notifications. HTTPS alone does not certify the store. Use virtual cards if your bank offers them.
protejeaza-card-bancar-cumparaturi-onlin.seo_title: How to protect your card when shopping online
protejeaza-card-bancar-cumparaturi-onlin.title: How to protect your bank card when shopping online
protejeaza-card-bancar-cumparaturi-onlin.meta_description: Check out the store, use payment authentication and bank notifications and react quickly to unknown transactions.
protejeaza-card-bancar-cumparaturi-onlin.content:
Paying online is safer when you verify the merchant, choose a suitable method and track transactions. Don't enter your card details just because the page has a lock in the address bar: HTTPS encrypts the connection, but doesn't prove the store is legitimate. A well-made ad or a very low price does not guarantee delivery or refund.

Check the store before payment

Access the site by typing the address or from a known source, check the full domain and search for contact details, delivery terms, return policy and merchant name. Search for the store name along with terms like "complaint" or "fraud." Reviews on the same site can be controlled by the seller, so check independent sources. Beware of sellers who remove you from the ad platform for direct payment.

Choose and authenticate payment

Use bank app authentication or 3-D Secure when offered and read the amount and merchant name before you approve. An authorization code is not a discount code; don't dictate it on the phone or enter it on an open page in a message. Virtual cards or temporary numbers can limit exposure to a merchant, if the bank offers them; check limits, fees and where it works.

Pay through the official platform and avoid hard-to-trace methods when the seller insists on bypassing the system. Keep order confirmation, conversations, invoice and terms offered. The ability to dispute a payment depends on the type of card, authorization, term and conditions of the bank or provider, so ask the issuer before buying if you have any questions.

Turn on notifications and check the extract

Enable payment notifications and periodically check transactions, including small amounts. A small charge can be a card check or an unauthorized transaction; don't guess, check in the bank's app. Temporarily block the card if the bank offers the function and contact the issuer via the number on the card or the official app when you see an unknown transaction.

Don't save your card on sites you don't use and protect the email that receives purchase confirmations. If you've entered your details on a fake site, contact your bank quickly, ask for a card block assessment and keep the URL for reporting. Avoid people who promise guaranteed money back against a fee.

ce-faci-dupa-ce-ai-trimis-bani-escroc.excerpt: Contact the bank or provider used for the transfer immediately, ask to stop or dispute the payment and keep the evidence. Recovery is not guaranteed and depends on the type of transaction and the method used according to the procedure.
ce-faci-dupa-ce-ai-trimis-bani-escroc.seo_title: Have you sent money to a scammer? Quick steps
ce-faci-dupa-ce-ai-trimis-bani-escroc.title: What to do if you sent money to an online scammer
ce-faci-dupa-ce-ai-trimis-bani-escroc.meta_description: Find out who to contact after a fraudulent payment, what evidence to keep and how to avoid refund scams.
ce-faci-dupa-ce-ai-trimis-bani-escroc.content:
Act immediately, even if you do not know if the payment can be stopped. Contact the bank or the service used for the transfer using the number on the card, the official application or the data found independently. Say you suspect fraud, indicate the amount and time, and ask if the transaction can be blocked, recalled or contested. The answer depends on the payment instrument, whether you authorized it and how long it has been; there is no guarantee of recovery.

What to do depending on payment

  • Card: ask the bank to evaluate the card blocking and charge dispute. Follow the steps and deadlines they tell you.
  • Bank transfer: immediately call the bank and ask to check the possibility of recall or blocking. Sends the transaction reference and recipient information.
  • Payment application: reports the payment in the application and contacts the card issuer or bank if the method is related to them.
  • Cryptocurrency, cash or voucher: the transfer may be very difficult or impossible to reverse. Contact the platform and keep transaction identifiers; do not pay "recovery fees" to intermediaries.

These are general categories, not a promise regarding the rules of a Romanian bank. Read the contract with the supplier and follow its instructions. If you authorized payment after being misled, explain exactly the circumstances; don't describe it as an unauthorized transaction if you confirmed it.

Keep the evidence

Save conversations, phone number, profile, website address, ad, receipt, payment reference and bank responses. Do not delete the account or continue negotiating with the scammer. If the platform allows reporting, do it after you've saved the useful information. Write down the persons contacted, the time of the call and the notification number.

Report and protect accounts

If you've submitted card details or credentials, secure your bank account and associated email, change reused passwords, and revoke unknown sessions. File a police report when you suspect a crime and consult DNSC for the cyber security component. Keep copies of evidence and only attach relevant information through official channels.

After the loss, fake recoverers may appear who claim to have found the money or know people from the bank. Don't pay upfront, give away codes, or install software remotely. A legitimate institution does not ask for your full password to process the notification.

cum-verifici-alerta-securitate-reala.excerpt: The alert can be genuine, outdated, taken out of context or fake. Confirm the message on the organization's official page, check the date and domain, and don't use the alarmist login link before verification.
cum-verifici-alerta-securitate-reala.seo_title: How to check if a security alert is real
cum-verifici-alerta-securitate-reala.title: How to check if a security alert is real
cum-verifici-alerta-securitate-reala.meta_description: Check the date, source, and links of a security alert before you share it, install something, or change your data.
cum-verifici-alerta-securitate-reala.content:
A security alert can announce a real vulnerability, a phishing campaign, or a product recommendation. Fake messages often copy the name of an institution and create pressure: "share now", "install this update" or "login to avoid blocking". Before you act, check if the alert also appears on the official page of the invoked organization.

Check issuer and date

Access the site by bookmarking or typing the domain, not the link in the message. Look for the alert title, reference number, affected product and publication or update date. An old recommendation may still be valid, but check for a newer version. Read if the alert comes from the manufacturer, a public institution, or a third party commenting on the alert.

Inspect required links and actions

An official message can contain links, but the domain must be the actual domain of the organization. Display name and HTTPS do not confirm authenticity by themselves. Don't install a file attached to an unsolicited alert or enter your password on an "account verification" page. If an update is recommended, open the manufacturer's updater app or tool directly.

Compare independent sources

Check if the manufacturer of the affected product has issued an advisory and if recognized authorities or response teams have reported the same. For Romania consult the DNSC channels; for European warnings, CERT-EU and ENISA publish resources and notices. Search by vulnerability identifier or alert number, but do not assume that popular results are official.

Do not amplify disinformation

If you don't find confirmation, don't redistribute the message with active links and don't automatically declare the alert false. You can ask the organization on an independently published channel or report the message to the platform. Remove personal data from captures before sharing. If you entered credentials or installed the file, follow the steps to secure your account and device and report the incident.

A credible alert typically describes the affected products or versions, the source, and mitigation steps. Even then, apply only the recommendations that suit your device and keep a backup before changes that can affect the system.

  • How to identify a fake site before entering personal data
  • How to recognize a fake email phishing

Useful sources and resources

  • CISA: security alerts and advisories
  • CERT-EU: security notices
  • DNSC: official incident reporting service

avertizari-oficiale-securitate-ciberneti.excerpt: For current information, consult DNSC, the product supplier and European sources such as ENISA or CERT-EU. Check the date, target audience and recommended steps before redistributing an important alert to others.
avertizari-oficiale-securitate-ciberneti.seo_title: Official sources of cyber alerts in Romania
avertizari-oficiale-securitate-ciberneti.title: Where to find official cyber security warnings in Romania
avertizari-oficiale-securitate-ciberneti.meta_description: Find alerts from DNSC, ENISA, CERT-EU and product providers and learn how to check their relevance.
avertizari-oficiale-securitate-ciberneti.content:
For an alert relevant to the public in Romania, start with the National Cyber ​​Security Directorate (DNSC) and the supplier of the mentioned product. It then compares with European sources, such as ENISA and CERT-EU, or with the cyber authority of the affected country. There is no single stream that covers all apps, vulnerabilities, and scams.

Romanian sources

The DNSC publishes information and provides incident reporting and guidance channels. The public service portal describes alert reporting and points to options such as 1911 and the DNSC platform; check the current page for availability, schedule and steps that apply to your situation. For a possible crime or injury, the Romanian Police is the right source for notification. A technical alert and a criminal complaint are not the same thing, and in some cases it may be useful to do both.

European sources and suppliers

ENISA publishes analyzes and materials on types of threats, and CERT-EU publishes technical advisories. These resources can be aimed at organizations and specialists, so check whether the recommendation applies to a home user. For a phone, browser or router, see also the manufacturer's official security page; affected versions and available updates appear there.

How to interpret a warning

  • Verify publication date and last update date.
  • Identify exactly the product, version and targeted group.
  • Separate urgent recommendations from technical context and optional measures.
  • Access links by typing the official domain or using saved bookmarks.
  • Do not submit codes, passwords or copies of documents to "verify" if you are affected.

Report without exposing others

Retains the message, URL, date and any technical reference. Before you post a screenshot publicly, hide your name, address, phone number, and codes. For reporting use the mentioned official service and follow its instructions; if money or accounts are at risk, contact the bank or account provider immediately.

Alerts evolve and a page can be updated or retired. Check the source on the day you act and don't treat an old news list as current information. This article is evergreen and does not state the existence of a recent incident.

black-friday-cum-verifici-un-magazin-onl.excerpt: Check the store, price, merchant details and payment method before a Black Friday order. Find out what signs may indicate a risky offer.
black-friday-cum-verifici-un-magazin-onl.seo_title: Black Friday: How to check an online store before you pay
black-friday-cum-verifici-un-magazin-onl.title: Black Friday: How to check an online store before you pay
black-friday-cum-verifici-un-magazin-onl.meta_description: Check the store, price, merchant details and payment method before a Black Friday order. Find out what signs can indicate a risky offer.
black-friday-cum-verifici-un-magazin-onl.content:
During sales, good deals appear alongside deceptive ads, stores imitating well-known brands, and pages designed to collect data or money. A big discount doesn't automatically mean the offer is a scam, but it's worth checking the store before entering your card details.

No quick check can guarantee that a merchant is trustworthy. If you find more alarm signs, stop the order and look for the product directly on the store's official website.

1. Check the exact address of the site

Look closely at the domain in the address bar. Scammers may use addresses that resemble a brand name but include extra words, hyphens, changed letters or unusual endings.

Do not open the store through a link received in an SMS, email or message on social networks. Search separately for the store name or manually type the address you already know.

Also check if the page uses HTTPS. The lock in the browser shows that the link is encrypted, but it does not prove that the store is legitimate. And a fake site can use HTTPS.

2. Search for merchant

's data

An online store should clearly state who sells the product and how they can be contacted. Look in the "Contact", "Terms and Conditions" or "About Us" pages:

  • company name;
  • head office address;
  • company identification data, such as CUI;
  • an email address and, if available, a telephone number;
  • information about delivery, returns and complaints.

Compare the displayed data with public company information. If they are missing altogether, are contradictory or you cannot identify the store operator, treat the order with caution.

A contact form or a free email address alone does not prove that the site is fraudulent. It matters the big picture and whether the information can be verified.

3. Compare price and discount

Search for the same product at several merchants. A large price difference may have legitimate explanations, but an offer well below the usual price, combined with an aggressive timer and lack of company data, is worth checking carefully.

Don't just rely on the discount percentage shown. Check:

  • final price, including shipping;
  • if the product is new, resealed or refurbished;
  • delivery term;
  • return conditions;
  • if the discount applies to the exact model and configuration you want.

Watch for messages that pressure you to buy immediately: "last chance", "only two products left" or a timer that resets when you reload the page.

4. Check reviews in multiple places

Reviews displayed right on the store page can be helpful, but they are not enough. Search for the store name along with terms like 'reviews', 'returns', 'order' or 'complaint'.

Look for patterns, not just a negative or positive comment:

  • many very similar reviews published in a short space of time;
  • repeated complaints about undelivered products or unpaid money;
  • reviews without concrete details;
  • store responses that do not clarify the issue.

Reviews can be fake or incomplete, so use them as a guide, not as the sole basis for your decision.

5. Choose payment carefully

Check that the payment page belongs to a known processor and that the displayed amount is correct before you confirm the transaction.

Do not send via email, SMS or private messages:

  • full card number;
  • CVV code;
  • PIN;
  • confirmation codes received via SMS or in the bank's application.

The bank will not ask you to disclose the authorization code to another person. Confirm the payment only if you initiated it and the details in the banking application match the order.

Cash on delivery can limit the risk of entering card details on the site, but does not guarantee that the product received will correspond to the description and does not eliminate all risks.

6. Read the shipping and return information

Before paying, check the estimated delivery time, shipping cost and return steps. For many online purchases, consumers have the right to withdraw from the contract within 14 days, but there are exceptions depending on the product or service.

Read the terms displayed by the merchant and keep the order confirmation, invoice and relevant conversations. If the return policy is unclear or appears to contradict the consumer rights information, ask for clarification before ordering.

Checklist before you press "Pay"

  • I checked the exact website address.
  • I have found and verified who the merchant is.
  • We have compared the price and model of the product.
  • We looked for reviews from independent sources.
  • I know how much the delivery costs and what the return conditions are.
  • I am not required to text card details or authorization codes.
  • I checked the amount and the merchant on the payment page or in the bank's app.

If several answers are "no" or the information contradicts itself, take your time. Close the page and search for the product on the merchant's official website or at a seller you can verify.

If you have already made a suspicious order

If you have entered your card details on a suspicious page, contact the bank immediately using the number in the official application or on the card. Ask to block the card if the bank recommends it and check recent transactions.

If you reused an account password on that site, change it on the other services where you used it. If you entered personal data or received suspicious messages after ordering, keep the evidence and do not access additional links sent by the alleged merchant.

For problems with a purchase, keep proof of payment, order confirmation and discussions with the seller. You can consult the information and notification channels published by National Authority for Consumer Protection (ANPC).
